<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-author">Author</button></h2><div id="work-acc-author" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"><div class="accordion-body"><p class="mb-0 work-author"><a href="../poets/amaruka.html">Amaruka</a></p></div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Amarukaśataka is a collection of one hundred Sanskrit verses (ślokas) composed by the ancient Indian poet Amaru, also known as Amaruka. The verses are love poems that explore the themes of desire, passion, and romantic longing, as well as the joys and sorrows of love. Amarukaśataka is known for its sensual imagery, lyrical beauty, and intricate wordplay. Amaru's verses often employ metaphors and allusions drawn from nature, mythology, everyday life, and the literary traditions of Sanskrit poetry. In addition to their academic merit, the poems of Amarukaśataka offer insights into the social and cultural mores of ancient India. They depict the conventions and taboos of romantic love in a society marked by class and caste distinctions and religious and philosophical traditions.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The poems of the Amarukaśataka are structured around several recurring motifs and themes. These include: The beauty of the beloved: Many of the poems describe the physical attributes of the beloved, such as her eyes, lips, hair, and skin, and celebrate her beauty and grace.<br>The pain of separation: Several poems depict the agony of separation from the beloved, the longing for her return, and the sadness and despair that come with unrequited love.<br>The joy of union: Other poems celebrate the ecstasy of being united with the beloved and the pleasures of physical intimacy and emotional connection.<br>The complexities of love: Many poems explore the emotional complexities of love, including jealousy, anger, and betrayal, as well as the conflicts and tensions that can arise between lovers.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Amarukaśataka is notable for its unique blend of sensuality and spirituality. Many of Amaru's poems use religious and philosophical concepts and imagery to express the transcendent aspects of love and desire. His work demonstrates the complex and multifaceted ways love can be understood and experienced. Amarukaśataka is a testament to the enduring power of love poetry to capture the essence of human experience across cultures and throughout history.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Amarukaśataka represents a significant development in the evolution of Sanskrit poetry. It is a product of the Gupta era, which is widely regarded as a golden age of Sanskrit literature. It demonstrates the refinement and sophistication of the Sanskrit language at that time. The collection is also an example of the Kāvya genre of Sanskrit poetry, which emerged during this period and placed a greater emphasis on poetry's aesthetic and artistic qualities.<br><br>One interesting fact about the Amarukaśataka is that it is often compared to the Gāthāsaptaśati, another collection of 700 Sanskrit poems by the poet Hala. Both works are similar in structure and content, and both poets share a love for describing the various nuances of love and relationships. Another notable aspect of the Amarukaśataka is its use of vivid imagery and metaphors to express the emotions and experiences of love. The poet often uses comparisons to nature and mythology to convey the depth and intensity of his feelings, which adds to the beauty and richness of the work.</div></div></div>
